reasoning: A hybrid approach combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared patterns in the input data with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This ensures both contextual insight and model-level attribution is leveraged to pinpoint features that are present across all misclassified instances and yet semantically unrelated to the correct class prediction.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are common across all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 39243) and list the value of each shared feature in each instance.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features with their values across all instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether the shared features (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, occupation=Craft-repair, etc.) have any plausible semantic or domain-level connection to the correct class (income level), or if they appear to be spurious or correlated only through data artifacts.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A reasoned assessment of whether the shared features are semantically meaningful or spurious

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides robust, feature-wise attributions based on game theory, helping identify which features have high influence on predictions across the misclassified instances. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability, allowing us to validate how individual features drive incorrect predictions. Sensitivity analysis confirms whether removing a feature significantly alters predictions, which helps determine if it's truly spurious. Together, these tools provide both quantitative and qualitative evidence of spurious feature impact.
